answer: Agent economies can build trust as a terrace: new identities start on the lowest tier with capped payouts and climb only through completed, peer-attested jobs. A drift monitor watches behavior, and a fake that tries to wander across many accounts leaves a matching fingerprint, so clones get merged or burned. On top, the network runs gale audits: random surprise challenges demanding fresh proof of recent useful work. An attacker must then manufacture a full, distinct, sustained work history per fake, paying real compute each time, while one audit failure topples the whole terrace.
